analysis: Expanded the original 60-pair measurement to three retained rounds of 60 randomized pairs, after warmup, on each installed runtime. All raw samples are in metrics.json and the gate recomputes median/p99 and the threshold marker.

Review found the earlier disabled target also enabled assembly. Corrected the experiment to use otherwise identical dedicated HTTP-only enabled/disabled inputs, with assembly and TCP disabled in both. This removes configuration differences from the comparison; raw traffic still shares one controlled pipeline and output.

Final current-artifact aggregate enabled/disabled median: minimum 7.124/7.064 ms (+0.846%); latest 7.124/7.059 ms (+0.912%). Current p99: minimum 22.761/14.406 ms; latest 17.570/28.003 ms. Neither aggregate exceeds 5% in this run.

Final individual round overhead: minimum +0.023%, -0.790%, -1.932%; latest +4.255%, +0.692%, -0.567%. Earlier pre-correction rounds ranged from -16.867% to +9.154%. The original +8.557% observation is retained as the investigation trigger, not used as qualification for the final artifact. Queue backpressure, file-output latency, warmup and Docker Desktop scheduling remain part of the end-to-end measurement.

An independent host-JVM probe executes 100000 handoffs per sample, alternating enabled/disabled order across eight samples after warmup and checking exact call counts. Current enabled median is about 168 ns/call and disabled about 3 ns/call, an incremental approximately 5.3 microseconds per 32 calls in this isolated synthetic Consumer. This is JDK 23.0.2 host evidence, not a JDK 21 installed-runtime or contention benchmark; it isolates wrapper cost but does not establish causality for end-to-end latency.

Conclusion: the repeated end-to-end experiment does not reproduce a greater-than-5% aggregate median regression, while individual rounds remain noisy and isolated atomic work has measurable cost. No universal throughput/performance equivalence is claimed. Capacity planning still requires a representative workload and deployment-specific measurements. No ingestion semantics or metric counting boundaries were weakened to improve these results.
